title: 웹 교수: 구성주의 온라인 교사의 딜레마

abstracts.value: The purposes of this study are to identify effective instructional strategies that online teacher educators can use for their distance education courses and to determine online teacher perceptions about which online instructional strategies are most effective for professional development courses. This study will also illustrate the disparities between the instructional strategies that are actually being used and those identified in the literature. We will also make recommendations based on our findings. Six instructors, who are teaching online professional development courses in the school of education of a mid-western university, were recruited for an individual and a focus group interview. The findings are categorized in four areas: 1) online teacher educators' perspectives, 2) the effect of students' professional experience on the instructors' methodology, and 3) instructional strategies actually used by online instructors. We found, in the majority of the interviews, that all of the online instructors had more or less constructivist perspectives; they were aware of teachers' needs, but this did not seem to largely affect the design and delivery of their online instruction. In reality, they developed their own strategies in a way somewhat different from the constructivist principles. We discuss what disparities exist, why they occur, and how to overcome them.
